directives.name: byte
directives.description: One byte per argument: an expression or a character literal (-1 is $FF).

directives.name: word
directives.description: 16-bit little-endian words; each argument is an expression. A relocatable symbol (lbl, lbl + n, lbl - n) gets a relocation in -c mode; a difference of two labels of one segment (end - start, end - start + 1) is a constant (see *Label expressions* under Relocatable Objects).

directives.name: dword
directives.description: 32-bit little-endian; each argument is an expression (a symbol: an R_LINEAR32 relocation with -c).

directives.name: long
directives.description: 32-bit little-endian; each argument is an expression (a symbol: an R_LINEAR32 relocation with -c).

directives.name: float
directives.description: 5-byte CBM floating point, rounded to nearest (.float 1.5 → 81 40 00 00 00; -1.0, 1.0e20).

directives.name: text
directives.description: PETSCII string (letters case-swapped: a-z → $41-$5A, A-Z → $C1-$DA; \n → $0D). Exactly one string argument.

directives.name: ascii
directives.description: Raw ASCII (\n → $0A).

directives.name: screencode
directives.description: Screen codes (@→0, A/a→1 …).

directives.name: res
directives.description: Reserve n bytes of fill (default 0); both are expressions. In .bss no bytes are emitted.
directives.example: .res n[, fill], .fill n[, fill], .space n[, fill]

directives.name: fill
directives.description: Reserve n bytes of fill (default 0); both are expressions. In .bss no bytes are emitted.
directives.example: .res n[, fill], .fill n[, fill], .space n[, fill]

directives.name: space
directives.description: Reserve n bytes of fill (default 0); both are expressions. In .bss no bytes are emitted.
directives.example: .res n[, fill], .fill n[, fill], .space n[, fill]

directives.name: align
directives.description: Pad to a multiple of n (n non-zero literal; fill an expression). In an object (-c) the padding counts from the object's part of the segment: ca45 exports the weak absolute cc45.align.text / .data / .bss (the largest n in that segment), so ln45 places that part on such a boundary ([lib45](../architecture/lib45.md)); zp and the far / bank sub-segments are not marked.

directives.name: balign
directives.description: Pad to a multiple of n (n non-zero literal; fill an expression). In an object (-c) the padding counts from the object's part of the segment: ca45 exports the weak absolute cc45.align.text / .data / .bss (the largest n in that segment), so ln45 places that part on such a boundary ([lib45](../architecture/lib45.md)); zp and the far / bank sub-segments are not marked.

directives.name: fillto
directives.description: Pad up to addr; error if already past it.

directives.name: incbin
directives.description: Insert a file's bytes (path relative to the current directory).

directives.name: import
directives.description: Insert a file's bytes (path relative to the current directory).

directives.name: array
directives.description: Reserve a zero-filled row-major array; see *Arrays*.

directives.name: basicupstart
directives.description: BASIC line 10 SYS addr (8 bytes plus the address's decimal digits: 12 for $080D, 13 for an address of 10000 or more); sets the origin to $2001 if no .org came first. A label defined *after* the stub is assumed to have 4 digits (an error says so if it has 5).

directives.name: org
directives.description: Set the program counter (an expression of symbols defined before it: * = base + $10).

directives.name: segment
directives.description: Switch segment; .segment "name" { … } switches back after the block. Text segments other than code (init, far — cc45's __far functions, which ln45 keeps in far memory) are text sub-segments of the .o45: references into them are relocated to their place in the object's text, and a call or jump into another segment is never shortened to a relative BSR/BRA.

directives.name: code
directives.description: Shortcuts for the segments code, data, bss. .segment "zp" holds base-page variables: in an object ln45 places them in the program's base page (see Relocatable Objects).

directives.name: data
directives.description: Shortcuts for the segments code, data, bss. .segment "zp" holds base-page variables: in an object ln45 places them in the program's base page (see Relocatable Objects).

directives.name: bss
directives.description: Shortcuts for the segments code, data, bss. .segment "zp" holds base-page variables: in an object ln45 places them in the program's base page (see Relocatable Objects).

directives.name: segmentorder
directives.description: Order in which segments are written (default init, code, data, bss, then the others in order of appearance, including default — the segment used before any switch).

directives.name: cpu
directives.description: The CPU the code is for, as --cpu (6502, 6510, 45gs02, _45gs02, 4510). Put it before the code. Other names (65c02, 65816) are accepted and ignored: the code is assembled for the 45GS02.

directives.name: const
directives.description: Constant; redefining it (or assigning it with =) is an error.

directives.name: var
directives.description: Assembler variable that can be reassigned; reassignments are tracked by position (++/-- change it by exactly one).

directives.name: global
directives.description: Export symbols from a .o45.

directives.name: weak
directives.description: Export as weak: a strong (.global) definition in another object wins at link time. In -c objects every reference to a weak *label*, also from the defining object, is relocated by name, so it reaches the strong definition when one is linked. A weak *absolute* symbol (.weak x / x = value) is used at its value in the defining object (so a base-page value keeps its base-page addressing); the object records the weak absolute symbols its code used (OPT_WEAKUSE), and ln45 refuses a program that defines one of them with another value (a default nothing in the object uses may be overridden freely). For a default that other code overrides, declare the symbol .extern where it is used and define the weak default in another object.

directives.name: extern
directives.description: Import symbols (value 0 until linked; one the file also defines, before or after the .extern, is that definition, as extern int x; int x; in C). An .extern base-page symbol is assembled as absolute. Only an object (-c) is linked: in a flat binary or .prg, using an .extern symbol that the source does not define is an error. An imported symbol can be used only in a form a relocation holds: sym, sym + n, n + sym, sym - n, < or > of those (as operands, .word/.long data); anything else (sym * 3, .word sym / 2), a use where the value is needed while assembling (.res, .fill, .align, .org, x = sym + 1), and a form the assembler cannot relocate (#(sym + 2), .byte <sym) are errors.

directives.name: local
directives.description: Name a frame offset for the .fp instructions.

directives.name: func_flags
directives.description: Function attribute flags: zp_call, stack_call, leaf, reentrant, static_alloc, zeroalloc, isr.

directives.name: reg_clobbers
directives.description: Registers not preserved.

directives.name: flag_clobbers
directives.description: Flags not preserved.

directives.name: zp_uses
directives.description: Base-page bytes read as parameters / overwritten / consumed: any of $00–$FF, recorded as the addresses themselves (#360; cc45.zeroPageStart does not change them); an address over $FF is an error (.zp_uses $100 is not a base-page address). ln45's stack-to-ZP bridge copies the parameter bytes up to the highest one .zp_uses names in $10–$2F.

directives.name: zp_clobbers
directives.description: Base-page bytes read as parameters / overwritten / consumed: any of $00–$FF, recorded as the addresses themselves (#360; cc45.zeroPageStart does not change them); an address over $FF is an error (.zp_uses $100 is not a base-page address). ln45's stack-to-ZP bridge copies the parameter bytes up to the highest one .zp_uses names in $10–$2F.

directives.name: zp_release
directives.description: Base-page bytes read as parameters / overwritten / consumed: any of $00–$FF, recorded as the addresses themselves (#360; cc45.zeroPageStart does not change them); an address over $FF is an error (.zp_uses $100 is not a base-page address). ln45's stack-to-ZP bridge copies the parameter bytes up to the highest one .zp_uses names in $10–$2F.

directives.name: frame_size
directives.description: Frame/activation record size (0–65535).

directives.name: param_sizes
directives.description: Parameter sizes in bytes (1–255).

directives.name: param_const
directives.description: Constant-argument hint for the linker.

directives.name: cleanup
directives.description: Add n bytes to the procedure's parameter size.

directives.name: frameptr_zp
directives.description: Base-page address of the frame pointer used by offset, sp and .fp accesses (default $FD).

directives.name: sac
directives.description: Mark the current procedure as statically allocated (compiler use).

directives.name: zpsym
directives.description: Base-page bytes start…start+len-1 stand for the linker-placed variable name (cc45 __zp globals; declare it .extern too). In -c mode every base-page operand in that range, in any procedure, gets an R_LOWX relocation against name (the offset in the range as its byte), and an operand of an instruction without a base-page mode (ldz, lda abs,y) an R_WORD against it: name is the variable's full address in the program's base page, so both reach the same byte. Ignored when assembling a flat binary.

directives.name: zar
directives.description: The procedure's own base-page bytes start…start+len-1 (cc45 uses $80). In -c mode every base-page operand in that range — plain, indexed, indirect, bbs/bbr, and inside simulated instructions — gets an R_LOWX relocation against the import <proc>__zar, with its offset in the block as the byte; ln45 defines <proc>__zar where it places the block (see ln45, base-page blocks). Ignored when assembling a flat binary.

directives.name: bptop
directives.description: The end of the register pool ($30–$7F) the object uses, $30–$80, instead of the one ca45 finds (see below). For code that names the ROM's page 0 while the base page is switched there (the library's float code reads the ROM's FAC at $63–$71 that way).

directives.name: bpindex
directives.description: The indexed base-page operands that follow ($nn,x, $nn,y, ($nn,x)) reach at most n bytes from theirs (0, the default: any byte above it), until the next .bpindex. cc45 says 5 around its float copies.

directives.name: loc
directives.description: Attribute following code to a source line (listings, -Roptimizer, debug info).

directives.name: dbg_var
directives.description: A C variable for a debugger (cc45 writes them after each endproc, and the module's after its data): an OPT_DEBUG_VARS entry in -c mode. A sym:NAME[+n] location is resolved to the object's segment and offset (seg:bss+12), an import (imp:NAME+n), an equate's value (abs:$XXXX) or none when the symbol is not defined (a local optimised away). No bytes. See lib45.md 1.12.

directives.name: dbg_type
directives.description: A struct / union layout for the debug types (OPT_DEBUG_TYPES; a long one goes on in further entries). No bytes.

directives.name: noopt_start
directives.description: The statements between them are left as written by every optimization pass (cc45's #pragma cc45 optimize(off)). The passes assume nothing about the registers after the region.

directives.name: noopt_end
directives.description: The statements between them are left as written by every optimization pass (cc45's #pragma cc45 optimize(off)). The passes assume nothing about the registers after the region.

directives.name: opt
directives.description: The statements between them keep their repeated runs inline (SeqExtract only; the other passes still run). For a hot routine or loop the rest of the file should still be made smaller around. Any other name is warned about and ignored.

directives.name: vtable_entry
directives.description: Compiler marker.

directives.name: function_sections
directives.description: Write a section table: one section per proc … endproc in a text segment, plus .split sections.

directives.name: overlay
directives.description: The object's code is in the code overlay name: exports cc45.overlay.name (ln45 [Code Overlays](ln45.md#code-overlays)).

directives.name: split
directives.description: Start a section in the current segment (text, data, BSS); it ends at the next .split/.nosplit of that segment or at the segment end.

directives.name: nosplit
directives.description: End the open section; what follows is residual (kept whenever anything of the object is).

directives.name: keep
directives.description: Always keep the current section (a root for ln45).

directives.name: ref
directives.description: The current section needs name (an import; no bytes, no relocation): ln45 links its definition only while the section is kept. Without sections it is an .extern. cc45 uses it for the printf digit hooks.
